chapters.introduction:
In a bustling startup office, rapid growth has made it hard to keep everyone on the same page.

The two colleagues were determined to find a way to improve communication and support each other through the chaos.

characters.name: Mara
characters.description: Mara, 28 is a front-end developer. She is introverted, detail-oriented, empathetic and often felt pulled in too many directions

characters.name: Leo
characters.description: Leo, 32, is a product manager, struggled to keep everyone aligned on priorities. He is extroverted, strategic thinker and empathetic

chapters.text: Mara comes in distressed: 'I cannot stand how disorganized our project communication is. I feel completely disconnected and unsupported!'
chapters.speechBubbleMara: I cannot stand how disorganized our communication is!

options.label: Mirror sentiment & clarify
options.fullLabel: Mirror their sentiment and ask clarifying question
options.shortText: It sounds like you're feeling overwhelmed.
options.feedback: Optimal: Actively listening, validating emotion, and inviting constructive elaboration builds deep trust.
options.dialog: Leo: 'It sounds like you're feeling really disconnected and unsupported because the communication has been so disorganized. Can you tell me more about what's been hardest for you lately?'
options.shortDialog: It sounds like you're feeling really disconnected and unsupported. Can you tell me more about what's hardest?
options.mara_reply: Mara: 'Thanks for saying that—it does feel like no one sees how scattered everything is. The hardest part is not knowing which tickets are actually priority, so I end up context-switching all day and still feel behind.'

options.label: Tell similar story
options.shortText: I've been in this situation before.
options.feedback: Sub-optimal: This filters their unique frustration through your past.
options.dialog: Leo: 'I totally get that. I felt the same way last quarter when we were switching tools. It was rough not knowing what was expected.'
options.shortDialog: I totally get that. I felt the same way last quarter when we were switching tools.
options.mara_reply: Mara: 'Yeah, I remember that too. For me right now it's more about not having a clear owner for decisions, so I'm waiting on answers from three different people and still not sure who has the final say.'

options.label: Offer quick fixes
options.shortText: Maybe we should reset the plan.
options.feedback: Premature Advice: They want understanding first.
options.dialog: Leo: 'We should just set up a daily stand-up and use a shared Kanban board. That usually solves communication issues.'
options.shortDialog: We should just set up a daily stand-up and use a shared Kanban board.
options.mara_reply: Mara: 'I get that those tools help, but honestly I'm more worried about why we keep changing priorities mid-sprint. A board won't fix it if the roadmap keeps shifting without telling us.'

options.label: Get defensive
options.shortText: It's not your fault / You're not paying attention.
options.feedback: Worst: You shut down psychological safety.
options.dialog: Leo: 'That's not fair. We send updates all the time. Maybe you're just not paying attention.'
options.shortDialog: That's not fair. We send updates all the time. Maybe you're just not paying attention.
options.mara_reply: Mara: 'That stings. I do read the updates, but they're often vague or contradictory. When I ask for clarity, I get told to "just figure it out," which makes me feel like my concerns don't matter.'
